# Cleveland Cavaliers Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-09-29, 34:41. https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE

## Summary

Josh Lloyd previews the Cleveland Cavaliers for the 26/27 fantasy season. His main concern is James Harden playing a full season next to Donovan Mitchell. In their minutes together last season, Mitchell's assists fell 18% and his usage dropped two points, so he does not see Mitchell as a first-round pick. He is also lower than most sites on Harden because of Harden's age and falling usage. He thinks Evan Mobley is fairly priced around pick 30 and still has upside, and he would fade Jarrett Allen at ESPN's rank of 49 but take him around 70 to 85. Peyton Watson is his top target, with a good minutes floor but limited usage. The bench is thin, especially at center, which makes Jaylen Tyson a late-round swing, Sam Merrill a streamer and Thomas Bryant a stash in deep formats. The Cavs have a bad fantasy playoff schedule with a two-game week and the most back-to-backs in the league.

## Rules and methods

- [5:17](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=317) Big men who split time between power forward and center usually put up better fantasy numbers at center: more blocks, more rebounds and a higher field goal percentage.
  > "if you are a big man and you're playing power forward and center, your fantasy numbers improve when you play center"
- [5:44](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=344) At power forward, a big man plays further out on the perimeter, relies more on his shooting and is not the only source of rim protection.
  > "If you're the four you're further out on the perimeter. You rely have to rely on your shooting"
- [30:48](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1848) The fantasy playoff schedule matters most for early picks. He does not want his best player to have a two-game week in the semifinals or championship.
  > "your best player will have a two-game week in your championship or semi-finals. And that is a no-go for me."
- [31:19](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1879) Schedule matters less for mid and late picks. He does not worry much about it when taking chances on later players.
  > "I don't care that much if I'm taking chances on Jarrett Allen or Jalen Tyson or Peyton Watson."
- [30:22](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1822) He recommends that fantasy leagues end on March 28th.
  > "If you play a league that ends on March 28th, my recommended end date, they play four games"
